mars_elev.procesado: Elevation = mean radius (MEGR) − areoid radius (MEGA), both at 1/16°. Mean of each 2×2 block → 1/8°, rounded to the meter (halves to even). Row 0 = 90°N, column 0 = 0°E; lat = 90 − (i+0.5)/8; lon = (j+0.5)/8.
mars_elev.nota: Not identical to MEGT (official MEDIAN topography): MEGR is the MEAN radius in the cell. Comparison at 1/8°: |diff| median 1.5 m, p99 35.2 m, max 535.0 m (on scarps).

fuente.cita: Smith, D. E. et al., MGS MOLA Mission Experiment Gridded Data Record (MEGDR), NASA Planetary Data System, MGS-M-MOLA-5-MEGDR-L3-V1.0, 2003.

mars_disparos.procesado: Sum of MEGC (shots per 1/16° cell) in each 2×2 block; stored capped at 255. 0 = the cell elevation is interpolated (no shots).

fuente.cita: Smith, D. E. et al., MGS MOLA Mission Experiment Gridded Data Record (MEGDR), NASA Planetary Data System, MGS-M-MOLA-5-MEGDR-L3-V1.0, 2003.

mars_inercia.procesado: Mean, in each 5×5 block of the 1/20° map, of the MEASURED pixels (interpolation mask ≠ 0 and inertia > 0). Blocks without any measured pixel = no data.
mars_inercia.nota: Derived range 5–5000; the map uses nighttime temperatures from 3 Mars years (1999–2004). At polar latitudes the value is affected by seasonal ices (see DATASET.CAT).

fuente.cita: Putzig, N. E. and Mellon, M. T. (2007), Apparent thermal inertia and the surface heterogeneity of Mars, Icarus, 191, 68–94. Data: MGS-M-TES-5-TIMAP-V1.0, NASA PDS.

moon_elev.procesado: Height = DN × 0.5 m (label SCALING_FACTOR) relative to a 1737.4 km sphere. Mean of each 2×2 block of 1/16° → 1/8°, rounded to the meter. Row 0 = 90°N, column 0 = 0°E; lat = 90 − (i+0.5)/8; lon = (j+0.5)/8.
moon_elev.nota: This is height relative to a sphere, not to the lunar geoid. The label declares MINIMUM/MAXIMUM -18150/21580 DN, but the file (MD5 verified) contains -17963/21371 DN.

fuente.cita: Smith, D. E. et al., LRO LOLA Gridded Data Record (GDR), NASA Planetary Data System, LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0.

moon_disparos.procesado: Sum of LDEC_16 (shots per 1/16° cell) in each 2×2 block; capped at 255. 0 = interpolated height.

fuente.cita: Smith, D. E. et al., LRO LOLA Gridded Data Record (GDR), NASA Planetary Data System, LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0.

moon_pendiente.procesado: Physical value = DN × 0.0015 + 45.0 (label); -32768 = no data. Mean of the valid cells of each 2×2 block of 1/16° → 1/8°. Stored as integer = value × 100.
moon_pendiente.nota: The label describes the product as slope “from a plane fit to three successive shots” with a variable baseline of 30 to 120 m, and the image description cites “a baseline of 240 meters”: the label itself is inconsistent; it is taken as slope at the scale of tens to hundreds of meters. Data from 2009–2011 (up to phase LRO_SM_17).

fuente.cita: Smith, D. E. et al., LRO LOLA Gridded Data Record (GDR), NASA Planetary Data System, LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0.

moon_rugosidad.procesado: Physical value = DN × 0.001 + 0.0 (label); -32768 = no data. Mean of the valid cells of each 2×2 block of 1/16° → 1/8°. Stored as integer = value × 1000.
moon_rugosidad.nota: Residual standard deviation of heights after fitting a plane to 5–15 returns from three successive shots (30–120 m baseline). Data from 2009–2011.

fuente.cita: Smith, D. E. et al., LRO LOLA Gridded Data Record (GDR), NASA Planetary Data System, LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0.

moon_h.resolucion: 0.5° (≈15 km); the instrument’s actual footprint is larger
moon_h.procesado: Copy of the published ASCII table (last column), reordered with north in row 0. It was checked to match the binary .dat version (value × 10) with a difference ≤ 1 unit.
moon_h.nota: Special product of the Lunar Prospector team hosted at the PDS Geosciences Node: the page itself warns that it is NOT a peer-reviewed PDS archive. It contains 4180 cells with negative (non-physical) values and 1 cell with a format overflow (“***”, left as no data). The source warns that the abundances “are not necessarily reliable in regions with high thorium and rare earth elements”.

fuente.mision: Lunar Prospector · neutron and gamma-ray spectrometers
fuente.cita: Feldman, W. C. et al. (2001), Evidence for water ice near the lunar poles, J. Geophys. Res., 106(E10), 23231–23251.

moon_tmax.nombre: Maximum bolometric temperature of the diurnal curve
moon_tmax.procesado: Mean bolometric brightness temperature (tbol) from nadir observations 2009-07-05 → 2015-04-01, binned by the source into 0.5° cells and 96 local-time intervals of 0.25 h. Maximum tbol among the local-time intervals with data.
moon_tmax.nota: Only some of the 96 local-time intervals have observations in each cell (see the number-of-intervals layer): the maximum and minimum are those of the observed intervals. At 0.5°, individual permanent shadows are not resolved.

productos: GLOBAL_CUMUL_AVG_CYL_<banda>_002.TAB (18 bandas de 10° de latitud), columna tbol
fuente.cita: Williams, J.-P. et al. (2017), The global surface temperatures of the Moon as measured by the Diviner Lunar Radiometer Experiment, Icarus, 283, 300–325. Data: LRO-L-DLRE-5-GCP-V1.0, NASA PDS.

moon_tmedia.procesado: Mean bolometric brightness temperature (tbol) from nadir observations 2009-07-05 → 2015-04-01, binned by the source into 0.5° cells and 96 local-time intervals of 0.25 h. Integral of the periodic polyline joining the intervals with data (linear interpolation in local time) divided by 24 h. It is only representative if the largest data gap is small (see the gap layer).
moon_tmedia.nota: Only some of the 96 local-time intervals have observations in each cell (see the number-of-intervals layer): the maximum and minimum are those of the observed intervals. At 0.5°, individual permanent shadows are not resolved.

Longest run of consecutive intervals without data (cyclic local time) × 0.25 h. 24 h = cell without any observation.

mars_neutrones.procesado: Copy of the EPITHERMAL NEUTRON FLUX column of the published table; 0 counts/s = no observations → no data. Longitude 0–360°E converted to −180…180°E.
mars_neutrones.nota: First 25.7 days of mapping (February–March 2002: northern winter). Over the north cap, seasonal CO2 frost masks part of the hydrogen signal, which is why the flux is high there. It is a neutron flux, not a concentration: it is not converted to % water.

fuente.cita: Feldman, W. C. et al. (2002), Global distribution of neutrons from Mars: results from Mars Odyssey, Science, 297, 75–78.

mars_h2o_aprox.nombre: Water equivalent (H2O) · APPROXIMATION at the poles
mars_h2o_aprox.metodo: Regression fitted where both data sets exist (1508 cells of 5°): ln(H2O %) = 3.694 -1.221·ln(epithermal neutron flux, counts/s); R² = 0.68, standard error ×1.16. Applied to the mean flux of each masked cell.
mars_h2o_aprox.nota: Calibrated with fluxes of 4.2–11.3 counts/s; 531 polar cells are outside that range (extrapolation): at the south pole it probably UNDERESTIMATES the ice. At the north pole the neutrons are from the winter of 2002, with CO2 frost on top, and the approximation comes out low.
mars_h2o_aprox.procesado: Only cells that the GRS team left without data; the rest is NaN. Regression fitted where both data sets exist (1508 cells of 5°): ln(H2O %) = 3.694 -1.221·ln(epithermal neutron flux, counts/s); R² = 0.68, standard error ×1.16. Applied to the mean flux of each masked cell.

fuente.cita: Approximation computed in this project (tools/construir_marte.py, aprox step).

mars_fe_aprox.metodo: Harmonic interpolation (Laplace equation) from the edge of the measured area: a smooth continuation of the mid-latitude values. There is no measurement at the poles for this element.
mars_fe_aprox.nota: It does not account for dilution by polar ice (which would lower the actual soil concentration). It is only a spatial continuation, not data.
